tldr: The paper proposes DAMCS, a decentralized multi-agent framework powered by LLMs with an adaptive hierarchical knowledge graph memory system and structured communication protocol, which outperforms both MARL and LLM baselines in cooperative open-world tasks.
contributions: Proposing DAMCS, a decentralized cooperative framework for generative agents combining an Adaptive Knowledge Graph Memory System (A-KGMS) and a Structured Communication System (S-CS)
Introducing the Multi-Agent Crafter (MAC) environment as a computationally efficient testbed for evaluating LLM-based multi-agent cooperation

Demonstrating significant efficiency gains through cooperative multi-agent planning, with a two-agent scenario achieving goals in 63% fewer steps and a six-agent scenario in 74% fewer steps compared to single-agent baselines
methods: The authors propose DAMCS in a novel Multi-Agent Crafter (MAC) environment modeled as a Dec-POMDP. Each agent maintains a multi-modal memory system with Short-Term Working Memory (sensory, episodic, feedback, retrospection) and Long-Term Memory consisting of an experience pool and a goal-oriented hierarchical knowledge graph that links experiences to goal nodes. An Adaptive Knowledge Graph Memory System enables agents to store, retrieve, and consolidate experiences dynamically. A Structured Communication System uses a Collaboration schema C_i = Φ(h_i, I_i, Δp_i) to ensure agents share only task-relevant information (observations, status, resources, goals, assistance requests) with specific target agents, following a hierarchical order where each agent assists the preceding one.
results: DAMCS outperforms both MARL and LLM baselines in task efficiency and collaboration on multi-agent open-world tasks. In the two-agent scenario, agents achieve the same goal with 63% fewer steps compared to single-agent scenarios. In the six-agent scenario, the reduction is 74% fewer steps, highlighting the importance of adaptive memory and structured communication for long-term goal achievement.
limitations: The framework is evaluated primarily on the newly introduced Multi-Agent Crafter (MAC) environment, and the paper does not report evaluations on other benchmark environments or real-world deployments. The paper also notes that traditional MARL/CTDE approaches face challenges with scalability to large numbers of agents and adaptability in non-stationary environments, though it does not extensively characterize DAMCS's own scaling behavior beyond the tested configurations.
